item.title: Drill 2026-10-14: crackme (bts bit-set)
item.description:
Crackme drill: find the passing input
Windows x64, ecx holds your 32-bit integer argument. The function returns 1 for the correct input:
xor eax, eax bts eax, ecx cmp eax, 100000h sete al ret
What is the smallest non-negative ecx that returns 1?
Answer: 20 (52, 84, ... also work)
1. xor eax, eax zeroes eax; bts eax, ecx ("bit test and set") sets bit number ecx in eax, so eax = 1 << ecx. 2. 0x100000 = 2^20, so only bit 20 may be set, giving ecx = 20. 3. With a register operand the bit offset is taken mod 32, so any ecx congruent to 20 mod 32 also passes (52, 84, even -12).
